result:
Phase 1 (App shell) is implemented and verified end-to-end on the iOS Simulator:

- **`app.config.ts`**: replaced the template's `main`/`second` entries with `main`, `health`, `transcribe`.
- **`src/pages/main/App.vue`**: Home screen — title, subtitle, `Health`/`Transcribe` buttons navigating via `sparkling-navigation`'s `router.open`.
- **`src/pages/health/App.vue`**, **`src/pages/transcribe/App.vue`**: static placeholders matching §3.2/§3.3 exactly (status line, enabled `Request Access`, disabled action button, empty states), each with a back link (`close()`) to Home.
- Removed the unused template `second` page.
- Added shared button/status/list styles to `src/App.css`.

One deviation worth flagging: the template's Home screen originally showed a logo image, but the Xcode project's synchronized resource group flattens PNGs under `Resources/Assets/static/...` to the app bundle root, breaking the `asset:///static/...` path the JS runtime expects (a pre-existing quirk, not something I introduced). Since the spec doesn't require a logo, I dropped it rather than fix an unrelated native asset pipeline issue.

Both `npm run build` and the `xcodebuild` Debug/iOS-Simulator build succeed, and I confirmed on-device (via `idb` taps) that all three screens render correctly and back-navigation works both ways.
